newsitem.title: SPAIN: Rato-Spain '98 budget less strict than '97 - press.
newsitem.headline: Rato-Spain '98 budget less strict than '97 - press.

text.p: Spain's 1998 budget will be strict, but less so than the 1997 budget, Economy Minister Rodrigo Rato said in an interview with financial daily La Gaceta de los Negocios on Monday.

The budget will be "restrictive, not as much as the 1997 (version) but restrictive. Restrictive means cutting the public deficit, because what we have demonstrated is that if the public deficit is reduced without hiking taxes, an economic expansion is produced," Rato said.
He added that European economic and monetary union is now more likely than it was a short time ago, with convergence in terms of inflation, deficits and growth already taking place.

"The possibility of a single currency is today much more intense than it was a few months ago...There is a decided political will in all countries to jointly form a single currency, because the only way to give Europe a global economic personality is to have an integrated financial system and an integrated and single monetary policy," he added.
